title: Every page needs a title
summary: The page has no title element, or it is empty. Add a short, unique title that describes the page, since it shows in tabs and search results.
problem: The page has no <title> element in its <head>, or the title is empty. The title is what appears in the browser tab, in bookmarks and as the headline of a search result.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear the title first when a page loads, and use it to know where they are. People with many tabs open, and anyone who bookmarks or searches, also depend on it. Search engines use it too.
whyItMatters: Without a title, browsers show the web address instead, which tells nobody what the page is. This is a WCAG 2.4.2 failure at Level A, the baseline that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
steps: Open the page template or theme file that prints the <head> section.
Add a <title> element inside <head> with a short, specific description of this page.
Put the unique part first, then the site name, such as Returns policy | Fernwood Garden Supply.
Make sure every page gets its own title, rather than one shared across the site.
before:
Returns policy

You can return unused items within thirty days.
after:
Returns policy

You can return unused items within thirty days.
howToCheck: Look at the browser tab, or view the page source and search for <title>. It should be present, not empty, and different from your other pages.
